subject: Resilience checklist & next steps for Skybridge pilot
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel King <daniel.king@skybridge.com>, Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@skybridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Resilience checklist & next steps for Skybridge pilot

Hi Daniel / Aisha —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps so we stay aligned. TL;DR: your primary goals are predictable availability under regional outages and graceful degradation of model quality/cost during peak/incident windows.

Pain points discussed
- Recent Q3 incident where primary region lost GPUs for ~18 minutes and traffic spiked; retries increased client latency by 2–3x.
- Lack of an automated model-fallback policy; teams have been manually switching to smaller models which increases human overhead and latency.
- No formal SLOs tied to customer-facing latency degradations — current playbook is ad-hoc.

Current stack (what you described)
- Inference hosted on single-region managed GPU pools (GCP us-west1)
- Two model families in prod: SkyGen-v2 (standard) and SkyLite-v1 (edge) — SkyLite is not actively deployed; used for batch only
- Traffic routed via internal API gateway that does not do model-level routing or prefix caching

Success criteria for pilot (agreed)
- Maintain 99.5% availability for inference requests (p95 latency < 600ms) across planned traffic profile
- Automatic model fallback so that during overload/outages requests succeed against a compatible variant with <10% reduction in downstream accuracy on defined eval set
- Proof of concept for cross-region failover with warm KV caching within a 5–15 minute warmup window

Proposed next steps (action items)
1) Redwood: share resilience checklist + pilot runbook (attached: resilience-checklist.xlsx) — includes failure-mode matrix, suggested fallbacks, and measurement plan. (Action: jasmine — sent)
2) Skybridge: share incident summary and current traffic profiles (RPS by minute, typical burst characteristics). (Action: daniel)
3) Redwood SE: propose initial fallback model mappings and region pairings; propose a 2-week canary test plan. (Action: monica)
4) Schedule technical run-through: propose Tue Dec 8 at 10am PT for SE-led design session. Confirm availability. (Action: all)

Open questions we flagged on the call
- Do you have hard contractual SLAs with any downstream customers that would restrict a temporary fidelity loss?
- Are there regulatory constraints on where inference can run for any subset of workloads (e.g., EU-only data)?

Attachments
- resilience-checklist.xlsx (failure-mode matrix, pilot measurement template)

If this captures things correctly, please reply with the requested incident summary and any edits to the success criteria. Happy to adjust.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:03:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Resilience checklist & next steps for Skybridge pilot

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the clear recap. This looks right. A couple clarifications and I've attached our incident summary for Q3. Highlights:
- Incident: 2026-09-14, us-west1 outage affecting our primary pool; we observed ~18 minutes of GPU unavailability with a 3x retry storm. Downstream SLAs were impacted for 22 minutes.
- Typical peak: 4.2k RPS sustained during end-of-month reporting windows; short bursts to ~12k RPS for ~2–3 minutes observed.
- We do have a handful of enterprise customers with contractual latency windows; any fallback policy must include a customer opt-out list.

Immediate asks from our side
1) Can Redwood indicate what the expected cost delta would be for keeping a warm cross-region failover (rough estimate per hour)?
2) We want to understand fidelity trade-offs: if we fallback to SkyLite-v1 (quantized), what's the expected drop on the key metric (accuracy@K) relative to SkyGen-v2?

I'm happy to share the full traffic logs via the Drive link if that helps. We'll aim to get you the traffic profiles by EOD Monday.

Regards,
Daniel King
CTO, Skybridge Financial
daniel.king@skybridge.com
+1 (617) 555-0199

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:10:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Resilience checklist & next steps for Skybridge pilot

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the incident doc. Quick technical read and initial plan that aligns with the success criteria. Notes below are an SE-level sketch to confirm before the design session.

Incident drivers we’ll mitigate
- Retry amplification: add request queueing + circuit-breaking at the gateway to prevent thundering herd.
- Warm KV cache: maintain async-replicated KV shards in secondary region (cold-warm policy) so first-token penalty is bounded.
- Model fallback: automatic mapping from SkyGen-v2 -> SkyLite-v1 (quantized int8) with token-level prefix caching preserved.

Pilot plan (2-week) — high level
- Phase 0 (prep, 3 days): sync on traffic profiles, deploy canary routing rules in us-west1 and warm us-east1 KV caches.
- Phase 1 (canary, 5 days): route 3–5% of traffic to fallback paths (observability on model divergence and latency).
- Phase 2 (stress, 4 days): simulate region loss with controlled capacity dip to validate failover within SLOs.
- Phase 3 (wrap-up, 2 days): measure success metrics, hand off runbook to Skybridge ops.

SLO proposals for pilot
- Availability: 99.5% successful responses for the baseline traffic profile
- Latency: p95 < 600ms for the primary route; during failover p95 < 1.2s
- Fidelity: target <10% drop on accuracy@K for the fallback model on the agreed eval set

I'll attach a short pilot runbook with steps and checkpoints (pilot-runbook.md). For your two asks:
- Cost delta: rough estimate for warm cross-region (US-EAST warm replicas) ~ +$0.12–0.20 per 1k requests depending on batching and caching hit-rate — we will model this with your traffic profile.
- Fidelity: early A/B on a sample eval suggests a 6–9% drop on accuracy@K when moving SkyGen-v2 -> SkyLite-v1 quantized; full eval pending.

Next step: can we lock in Tue Dec 8 10am PT for the design session? Send a calendar invite and we’ll prepare the runbook walkthrough.

Best,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference

Attachments: pilot-runbook.md
